questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always wanted to explore nz both in terms of culture and especially (!!) in terms of the nature. Since nz is literally on the other side of the world, and you can't naturally just pass by + considering the environment, I wanted to stay for a longer period of time and an exchange seemed like the perfect opportunity:) Also, I really wanted to go to an english-speaking country, so there wouldn't be a language barrier and I could easily communicate with the locals.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nz is literally the most amazing and beautiful place on earth. I wish for everyone to go there and I can't believe I had the privilege to live there and get to experience their culture:') GO!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In general, vuw's website is extremely helpful and if in doubt about anything, they respond really fast on their email. They have an entire team only focusing on their international students and they guide you through most. That said, there's a ton of things that you need to have taken care of before arriving, but it's definitely manageable and you can always email them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I lived in a campus dorm, there's a lot of extra assistance and guidance. I was picked up in the airport, had a welcome team, there were events and food in the first week (and the rest of the trimester) and I feel like if I had any requests, my RA or head of hall would do anything to help me:)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were so many events, also specifically directed towards international students - Nz get a lot of internationals and vuw were generally really aware of us and our well-being, KU take notes<3

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I really thought of finding private housing as I've heard that it was cheaper and on-campus housing generally attracted younger students. BUT I quickly realised that it was wayyy easier just applying for a dorm on campus and not necessarily more expensive. There are quite a few dorms only for mature students (20+) which are self-catered (you cook yourself) and there's both kiwis and internationals. You are guaranteed a place if you apply early and you are taken very well care of + meet a ton of other students really easily. I personally didn't go to a lot of the events they plan and didn't use the well-being coach or got help, as I was pretty self-sufficient lol, but it is nice to know that there are someone looking after you:)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had my own (bigger) kitchen which I shared with 5 other people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived at Everton Hall and was really satisfied:) I lived in a villa-ish place with 5 other kiwis and it was 5 min. from Kelburn campus and 10 min from cbd. My flatmates were sooo sweet, all 23+ and we ate together 5/7 days a week. At Everton (and other uni halls) they look at what you've written about yourself in your accommodation application, and then match you with your future roommates - so it's good to write a nice application for your own sake.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The villas/flats at Everton and in nz in general are really badly isolated, so make sure to bring warm socks. Also there's a ton of well-being support available and they really worry and take care of you.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you read the emails thoroughly and apply by the deadlines there shouldn't be any problems.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to register as a student and then apply for courses after. I honestly don't remember the process in detail, but there were quite a few things you needed to do, but I had no issues at all.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: EMAIL! They are so good at replying and helping.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my first choices, but know of people who had to re-apply.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it fairly quickly so you know early if you have any issues or need to change courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Honestly, I didn't go to nz for the academics:) So I just wanted to have fun and if I learned something new along the way I was happy.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had heard that the courses were really easy compared to KU, but that was not necessarily my experience lol. It is definitely different and you don't have 1 big project by the end of the trimester, like I've had in DK, but a lot (!!) of smaller assignments. I feel like it really depends on your lecturer and their style. I had two first year courses and one second year course, and while one course was extremely easy, the other two were quite rough due to my lecturers and their expectations:))

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Like I mentioned, vuw tend to have a lot of smaller assignments/quizzes spread out over the tri, kinda like gymnasiet. It was rough getting used to, as there are many assignments due at the same time and you don't really know what the level is or what your lecturer expects. In hindsight I could've relaxed a lot more, as it is pass/fail when you're on exchange..

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Film206: Hollywood Cinema (I took this course because I read that Tim Groves was amazing. I really didn't think so, but it was honestly a refreshing course as it was contemporary films)
Film102: Film movements (As much as I disliked Tim Groves, I loooved this lecturer Missy Molloy - a feminist icon<3)
Maor123: Te Iwi Māori me āna Tikanga/Māori Society and Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Maor123: Te Iwi Māori me āna Tikanga/Māori Society and Culture!!!
This course was amazing. When in nz, I encourage everyone to learn about the maori culture and potentially learn a bit of te reo. It was a tricky course in the beginning, as you need to figure out what all the different words mean and learn about a complex history and culture. But it was sooo rewarding and interesting and honestly added so much more to my exchange and relation to nz<3

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I drank a lot more than I expected haha. Going out every weekend wasn't on my to-do list in nz, but it was fun and a nice way of relaxing after a busy week.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee and eating out is a looot cheaper. Groceries are the same or a bit more expensive than dk. Vegetables were quite expensive in the beginning (july/august) but as summer came closer, the price dropped. Also, there's a vegetable market every sunday by the waterfront, and there, there's money to save.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any clubs really, but there were a looot of opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's literally so many clubs and an expo in the beginning of the tri, where you can meet them all and join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Welly is a really cultural city and there are a ton of nice shops and cafes, so I spent a lot of time just hanging out and exploring the city. It is fairly walkable, the streets are just steeeep and it is windy;)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I wish I spent more time going on smaller trips outside of welly in the weekends, because everytime I did, it was the best thing ever. My flatmate invited me to stay with her and her family in Whanganui for a weekend, which was niicee. We went on a hike to the escarpment track (1-day hike), went to a rugby match (that's a must-do), visited Zealandia, and I spent a lot of time in the botanical garden which is just by Kelburn Campus.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy. Kiwis are so freaking nice and easy-going + so open and interested<3 And Welly is just an amazing city, by far the nicest in nz (no bias), but nz is known for its shitty cities, and Welly is NOT one of them - it's full of culture and good vibes, though the cafes close at 15 (??)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: honestly, as I took two first year courses, the students were usually 18/19, so I didn't really hang with them. I was lucky to live with older local students so I spent time with them, but mostly I got international friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, the cafes close early and so do the clubs. Also, you can't really go anywhere without a car, as the public transportation is quite shit. So either buy one (they're cheap), rent one, or team up with someone who has a car, if you feel like exploring the country.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The natureeeee!!! so freaking beautiful. Their appreciation of their ancestry - Maori, their consideration of other people and the environment<3

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The preparation is a lot, but definitely worth it. I was so stressed in the spring, but it all worked out. 
2. The tri (tri 2) usually finish mid/end october, and I ended up staying until beginning of Jan, as I wanted to travel further, and it was the best decision ever. 
3. Don't stress about the academics. I def stressed way too much and that took away a lot of my time in Welly. It doesn't matter if you get an A+ or C-

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I worked for a month at an orchard close to queenstown after I finished my time at vuw, and it was amazing BUT I had to apply for a holiday working visa and that ended up costing a lot, cause I had to get a chest x-ray.. just worth thinking about if that is the plan, cause I really didn't know I had to do that.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: ah everything.. the people, the nature, the culture. It was freaking amazing and I really hope i get to go back at some point. it was a solid 10/10 and the perfect mix between living in a smaller big city, studying and learning about the culture, and then travelling and really experiencing amazing nature afterwards<3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I left 30/6, just before the summer break and therefore didn't have any break before starting a new trimester. All of my friends back home were at festivals and enjoying their summer, while it was winter in nz and I just started school again. That was tough, but finishing in october and travelling for two months during nz summer made up for it x100.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO TO NEW ZEALAND!!! It is expensive and faaar away, but sooo worth it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
